jason (cust): Hey team — running into a weird one from a customer private VPC behind their corporate proxy. Streaming responses from our hosted API get truncated ~500–700 bytes, then the socket is closed. Works fine from home network. Happens only from office.

maya (support): Thanks @jason, can you confirm this is via HTTP CONNECT tunneling (proxy intercept) to api.redwood.cloud? any error codes in client logs?

jason (cust): Yep CONNECT to proxy:8080 -> tunnel to api.redwood.cloud:443. Client shows a partial stream (first chunk) then `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`. No 4xx/5xx, just abrupt close. Happens on both curl and our app.

maya (support): Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and a tcpdump/pcap excerpt if available? Also which proxy vendor/version?

jason (cust): Repro: ```curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 -N "https://api.redwood.cloud/v1/streams?model=gpt-3.5" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"``` Output: we get initial event(s) then socket closes. tcpdump shows TLS ClientHello then server sends ~600 bytes of application data then FIN from proxy. Proxy vendor = "CorpDLP 3.2" (appliance).

leo (eng-infra): Interesting. Two quick hypotheses: 1) MITM TLS inspection appliance terminating CONNECT and re-issuing TLS with different ALPN/SNI leading to mismatch for our streaming runtime (we rely on h2/ALPN and continuous frames). 2) Middlebox truncating TCP segments (DNP/DLP clipping) or forcibly terminating long-lived tunnels after first data burst.

priya (eng-runtime): Streaming uses HTTP/2 with server PUSH-like chunking and long-lived connections + TLS 1.3. If proxy re-terminates TLS and strips ALPN or rewrites SNI, the runtime may detect incompatible transport and close to avoid token leakage. Do we have the exact clienthello from the pcap? look for TLS extensions (alpn, sni).

jason (cust): Added the clienthello hex snip: ```ClientHello alpn: http/1.1 sni: api.redwood.cloud cipher: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 extensions truncated at 512 bytes``` Looks like ALPN is http/1.1 (proxy probably downgraded).

maya (support): That ALPN downgrade is a smoking gun. Our streaming endpoint expects h2 ALPN. If the proxy forces http/1.1 the connection will not behave as expected — streaming frames may be treated as body bytes and connection torn down.

leo (eng-infra): Action items: 1) Confirm whether the appliance is doing TLS inspection (terminating CONNECT). 2) Ask customer to test direct TCP CONNECT to the origin IP bypassing proxy (if allowed) — quick check: `curl --proxy "" --resolve api.redwood.cloud:443:54.23.12.34 https://api.redwood.cloud/..` 3) If that works, recommend allowlisting SNI/hostname or enable SNI passthrough on the DLP appliance.

jason (cust): I tried bypassing proxy from a test VM (no proxy) — streaming is stable. So bypass works. Customer says they can request exception but wants minimal config change.

priya (eng-runtime): Temporary mitigation: we can offer a dedicated IP that they can allowlist in their egress firewall so the CONNECT goes straight to our IP and the proxy may be able to do blind TCP pass-through. Long-term: require SNI passthrough or disable TLS inspection for api.redwood.cloud for customers using streaming.

maya (support): I'm going to raise an enterprise support ticket with recommended wording for the customer's security team: ask them to allow TCP CONNECT passthrough to api.redwood.cloud:443 or exempt api.redwood.cloud from TLS inspection. I'll include our sample pcap snippet and the curl repro.

jason (cust): That would be great. One more question — is there any header we could set client-side to avoid inspection? e.g., force `Connection: keep-alive`?

leo (eng-infra): Most TLS-inspection appliances break at the TLS layer; HTTP headers won't help because inspection is upstream. Headers are visible only after TLS is established. If the proxy is terminating TLS, it can rewrite ALPN/SNI regardless of headers.

priya (eng-runtime): Also adding: if the appliance truncates ClientHello size (some DLPs do to limit TLS extension parsing), that can cause handshake failures or fallback to http/1.1. If possible ask their security team to allow full ClientHello or enable a passthrough profile.

maya (support): Escalating to eng-runtime with label: `support/priv-vpc-proxy-inspect` and attaching pcap + timeline. Eng, can you run quick check on whether our streaming servers detect ALPN mismatch and log a distinct reason code? If so we can provide that to customer to show evidence.

priya (eng-runtime): Will look now. If we log `alpn_mismatch` or `client_terminated_conn` we can pull logs for that timeframe. Also happy to provide a dedicated IP for allowlisting — @maya please share the customer org id.

jason (cust): Org ID 7654. Thanks — please include step-by-step wording for security team. They require exact config changes.

maya (support): Copying suggested wording: "Please configure your edge DLP/proxy to allow raw TCP CONNECT passthrough to api.redwood.cloud:443 (or exempt api.redwood.cloud from TLS inspection). Ensure SNI passthrough is enabled so the upstream TLS ClientHello reaches our origin unaltered. If allowlisting by IP, allow 54.23.12.34 and 54.23.12.35 (note: these are sample IPs; confirm with Redwood support)." :thumbsup:

leo (eng-infra): I'll add: If they cannot disable inspection, ask them to preserve ALPN=h2 and SNI header for the CONNECT target. Some appliances have a "passthrough for TLS-ALPN-sensitive hosts" profile.

jason (cust): I'll forward to their security team and request exception. Thanks all. Please keep the ticket open until confirmed.

albion-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026-412 created and assigned to eng-runtime.

maya (support): Leaving this open, will update once customer confirms security change. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
